methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective registry-based cohort includes non-metastatic TNBC cases from 2014–2020 (n=149) with androgen receptor (AR) status assessed by standardized IHC on diagnostic biopsy tissue (Ventana Benchmark Ultra; SP107 clone; positivity threshold >1%). Survival endpoints (DFS, OS, BCSS) are defined and analyzed with Kaplan–Meier/log-rank tests and Cox regression, with follow-up summarized using reverse Kaplan–Meier (median 61.6 months). The study is limited by modest sample size, retrospective confounding (including treatment selection and surgery type), and reliance on a single IHC cutoff without molecular subtyping.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The question is clinically relevant because AR expression is a plausible prognostic/predictive biomarker and potential therapeutic target in a subset of TNBC. In this cohort, AR positivity (36.7%) was not associated with DFS or BCSS and was not significant in univariable or multivariable Cox models for OS/DFS (e.g., OS HR ~0.71 univariable and ~0.65 multivariable, both non-significant). The results mainly support the conclusion that AR IHC status alone is insufficient as a prognostic marker in this setting, rather than changing treatment decisions.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports the biomarker assay (platform, antibody clone, fixation/antigen retrieval conditions, and the >1% cutoff) and defines time-to-event outcomes and key statistical methods (Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Cox regression). It also reports follow-up duration and provides concrete survival estimates and hazard ratios for AR and major clinicopathologic factors (tumor size, nodal status). However, REMARK-style reporting is incomplete in the provided text (e.g., handling of missing data, pre-specification of covariates, and full model diagnostics are not clearly described), and there is no explicit data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Many prior studies and meta-analyses have evaluated AR expression and prognosis in TNBC, and this manuscript largely contributes additional cohort data rather than a new mechanistic or methodological advance. The main incremental aspect is the regional cohort context (Levant area) with standardized IHC and follow-up. Overall, the work is confirmatory and addresses variability in reported AR prognostic effects.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with explicit cohort description, assay details, and straightforward presentation of the main finding that AR status is not prognostic in this dataset. Results are presented with concrete 5-year survival estimates and follow-up quantification, and limitations are openly discussed (cutoff choice, sample size, residual confounding). Some interpretation around late convergence of survival curves is speculative, but the overall presentation is coherent.

key_strengths: Clear biomarker assay description (SP107 IHC on whole tissue sections; >1% cutoff) and defined survival endpoints (DFS/OS/BCSS) with time-to-event analyses.
Reports follow-up using reverse Kaplan–Meier (median 61.6 months) and provides both univariable and multivariable Cox estimates for AR and clinical covariates.
Negative result is presented transparently, aligning multivariable findings with the conclusion that AR status is not prognostic in this cohort.
key_concerns: Modest sample size and retrospective confounding (treatment and surgery type associations) limit power and interpretability for a prognostic biomarker claim.
Single IHC cutoff without molecular LAR subtyping may misclassify biologically relevant AR-driven TNBC subsets.
Reproducibility limitations (no explicit data availability statement; limited detail on covariate selection and missing data handling in the provided text).
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent single-center retrospective prognostic biomarker analysis with a clear negative conclusion, but limited novelty and residual confounding/power constraints make it most plausible for a lower-tier outlet after revisions that strengthen reporting and robustness.
